What the mark floor says about a nav glyph (G). The shipped mark is drawn 372px wide, at which its thinnest stroke lands 2.02px. Its thinnest stroke is 1.3 viewBox units, so a 1px floor (D119) needs the mark at least 184.6px wide. At 24px the gate measured the strokes at 0.21px, and the mark probe — which reads the first svg[data-mark] on the page — took the glyph for the hero mark and failed 37 checks. A nav glyph is possible only as its own thing with its own rule, not as the mark.

4. The copy the page says twice

Sentences are compared on content words only, split at terminal punctuation (not at semicolons — this page writes its repeated claims as semicolon pairs). A pair is reported when it shares at least 3 content words and either Jaccard ≥ 0.45 or overlap ≥ 0.5. Jaccard is shared vocabulary over union; overlap is how much of the shorter sentence is inside the longer one.

5. Deleting one side of each pair — every option is a deletion, not a reword

Copy here comes from `src/content.json` and ruled strings, so a priced option can only remove an exact sentence. Rewording is a ruling first, and an option that reworded would be pricing the builder's words, not the club's.

6. What this round cannot yet answer

a. `name-lockup` and `descriptor-owns-display` pass the shipped render gate, but `npm run check:copy` reads source, and the round mutates the built page. Neither has been run against the copy gate; both move the descriptor between slots, which is exactly what `slot-coupling` exists to catch.
b. No `design/copy-duplicates.json` baseline exists yet, so `check:content`'s `near-duplicate-surface` rule currently carries its exemptions in code. Run `node scripts/check-content.mjs --print-baseline` and rule each pair open or accepted.
c. The gate verdicts for `chrome-ground` and `dup-homework-band-goes` were re-run after a probe flake (a headless Firefox that never posted); both are now clean, with the retry count in the record.
